oai_dc:dc.dc:title: The Humanist Roots and Anthropological Valences of Gadamer's Hermeneutics
oai_dc:dc.dc:creator: Alcaine, Sofía
oai_dc:dc.dc:subject: Gadamer
hermeneutics
philosophical anthropology
humanism
Menschenbild
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Despite the numerous references to the Grundzüge des Menschen (essential features of the human being) and a certain Menschenbild (conception of the human being) throughout Gadamer’s works, the anthropological dimension of his thought has thus far received little systematic attention in Gadamerian scholarship. This article traces the connection between Gadamer’s adherence to the humanist tradition and the anthropological valences of his philosophy. The first part offers a genealogy of Gadamer’s humanism – from its roots in Renaissance Italy through the classicism of the 19th and 20th centuries – and identifies some of the most salient humanist elements in Gadamer’s thought. The second part argues that Gadamer’s hermeneutics is inherently anthropological, insofar as it studies the lifelong quest for (self-)understanding that constitutes human existence. This article is conceived as an initial contribution to a broader project elucidating Gadamer’s Menschenbild, and seeks to encourage other Gadamer scholars to join the conversation around this topic.
oai_dc:dc.dc:source: Journal of Gadamer Studies; Vol. 1 No. 2 (2026): Language, Virtue, Friendship and Communal Practice
